title: Proving the Reflection Identity ceiling(-x) = -floor(x)
originalTopic: The Greatest and Least Integer Functions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Determine whether the identity ceiling(-x) = -floor(x) holds for all real numbers x, and provide a rigorous mathematical justification.

steps.title: Bound x Using Its Floor Integer n
steps.mathExpression: n = \lfloor x \rfloor \iff n \le x < n + 1, \quad n \in \mathbb{Z}
steps.explanation: Let x be any real number and let n = floor(x). By the definition of the greatest integer function, n is the unique integer satisfying n <= x < n + 1.
steps.why: Every real number x lies in a unique half-open unit interval [n, n + 1) with integer endpoints.

steps.title: Negate the Compound Inequality
steps.explanation: Multiply the inequality n <= x < n + 1 through by -1, which reverses both inequality signs and places -x in the half-open interval (-n - 1, -n].
steps.why: Multiplying a valid inequality by -1 reverses the order relation.

steps.title: Apply the Definition of the Ceiling Function to -x
steps.explanation: Since -n is an integer and (-n) - 1 < -x <= -n, -n is by definition the least integer greater than or equal to -x. Substituting n = floor(x) proves ceiling(-x) = -floor(x) for all real x.
steps.why: The unique integer m satisfying m - 1 < y <= m is ceiling(y); here y = -x and m = -n.
